title: The design rules say what the video mock says about the Animating list
goal: The shared design rules still say the panel beside a video's timeline lists every value that could be animated, and name the video mock as the model for that. The user's video mock was put back on 2026-09-23 and now lists only what is animating, with an Animate a property button for the rest, and the app shipped exactly that on 2026-09-25. A runner who reads the rule will build the old list back and fight the mock, so the rule has to say what the mock says.
notes: Found by the 2026-09-25 digest design review. docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md line ~2134 (D10 heading 'A property list shows what CAN be animated, not what is') and its last paragraph: '`pages/video.html` remains canonical for the printed catalogue. It is the CLIP spelling'. Against it: docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html line ~844 ('The pane lists what this clip IS animating; everything else is one click') and ~875 (Animate a property button), restored by 823fc26d; shipped by b009ac43 (the-properties-pane-opens-on-the-clip-line-and-l, audit queue/audits/2026-09-25-properties-pane.json). The mock is the floor: change the rule, never the mock.
acceptance: Rule D10 in the shared UX patterns doc says a video clip's panel lists only what the clip is animating, with a searchable Animate a property picker for everything else, and names the user's video mock as the reason

D10 keeps what it exists to protect, written against the new spelling: the way to animate something is on screen before anything moves (the picker button and the 'nothing yet' line), and removing the last key never makes a value unreachable
No other place in the shared docs (UX-PATTERNS D10 and D17, AGENTS.md, docs/design/video.md) still calls video.html the printed catalogue
The runner of a-moving-layer-shows-between-the-keys-in-propert can read one answer for where Curve and Path live, or the rule says plainly that the two mocks disagree and points at that task's card

The shared guide rule (D16) also says a guide never draws a closed rectangle, because a closed outline is the app's word for what you picked, and what to draw instead (a wash filling a band, or hairlines running off the edge), citing queue/audits/2026-09-20-icon-keylines-read-as-guides.json; nothing else in the doc shows a guide as a closed box

The shared rules say once what happens when a mock prints a sentence longer than the panel (40 characters) or chrome (30 characters) budget the user picked: the budget wins, the sentence moves behind the question mark beside its header, and the audit names it

log.note: triage 2026-09-26: folded in the-guide-rule-says-that-a-guide-never-closes-a (p3 since 2026-09-20): the same document, the same kind of scrub, one runner pass. Its acceptance is the last item here.

triage 2026-09-27: one more rule to settle in the same pass. Three audits this cycle had to choose between a sentence the mock prints and the user's no-sentences answers (40 characters in the panel, 30 in the chrome): 2026-09-27-panel-labels-not-sentences put 'drag the diamonds on the lane' and 'Any property can be keyed' behind question marks, 2026-09-27-new-empty-video left out the mock's empty-timeline hint and asked the user. Each runner decided alone. The rules should say once which wins and where a cut sentence goes (the question mark), so the next runner does not re-decide it.

Checked each rule against its source: video.html renderProps (Animating header 'N of 13 properties' / 'nothing yet', rows with diamond and ×, Animate a property picker, grouped and searchable), a-moving-layer-shows-between-the-keys-in-propert (done 2026-09-27: Curve and Path in a Between the keys section under Animating), the two 2026-09-27 audits for the sentence-budget cases. Rewrote D10, the checklist line, AGENTS.md's D10 bullet and docs/design/video-surface.md item 5 (the only other doc calling video.html a printed catalogue; docs/design/video.md never did). D16 gains an explicit 'never a closed rectangle' bullet. §4 gains 'When the mock prints a sentence longer than the budget'. The runner prompt's 'a line printed in the mock ships as drawn' contradicted that answer, so it now points at the same rule. Scripts/test.sh green (10,139 tests).
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

left rough: docs/design/video-surface.md item 3 still says 'Fixed: rows are layers', which D18's 2026-09-23 rewrite withdrew; the doc's own read-first banner already says the tracks came back, so it misleads nobody who reads the top. Not filed.

UX-PATTERNS v2.4 (commit 4225c023): D10 now says a clip's Animating list shows only what it animates, with an always-present searchable Animate a property picker, names video.html as the reason, keeps both obligations (door on screen before anything moves; last key goes back to the picker), and says Curve and Path live in Between the keys. D16 bans a guide's closed rectangle, citing the 2026-09-20 keylines audit. New §4 rule: the budget wins over a long mock line, which moves behind the section question mark or the control tip, and the audit names it. AGENTS.md, video-surface.md and the runner prompt follow. Docs only; Scripts/test.sh green.
